manifest.name: dsh-plugin-session-token-stats
manifest.description: Token usage, estimated cost and budget, per-session breakdown, and live CPU/memory monitoring for every stored DSH session.
manifest.author: genius-alray

bundle.text:
# Adds only this plugin's row. No official DSH component is overridden.
- insert:
    - id: session-token-stats
      name: 'dsh-plugin-session-token-stats'

readme.text:
**English** | [中文](./README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web plugin that turns your real session logs into a token-usage dashboard: total tokens, session count, a daily usage timeline, per-session breakdown with cache-hit rate, and live CPU/memory monitoring.

It counts tokens only. There is no reliable billing API for these sessions, so the page deliberately shows **no estimated cost and no budget** instead of presenting a guess as a fact.

- **Summary cards** — total tokens (uncached input / cache-hit input / output), sessions (turns plus how many subagent sessions were merged), tokens used this month, and the overall cache-hit rate.
- **Token timeline** — daily stacked bars for the last 7 / 30 / 90 days (uncached, cache hit, output). Hover a bar for that day's exact counts; the range is a per-browser setting.
- **Per-session usage** — one row per **main conversation**, newest first. Subagent sessions are merged into the conversation that spawned them (the whole `parentSession` chain is folded, including multi-level delegation) and never listed separately. Select a row to expand the per-model breakdown, merged subagent count, creation/last-activity timestamps, and session id.
- **CPU & memory** — system CPU usage with a 120-second sparkline, 1/5/15-minute load average, DSH process CPU and RSS, system memory, core count, process uptime, and host identity.

The Host half reads durable session logs through `ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions()` / `readSession(id)` and counts every `assistant/message` usage report:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| uncached input | `usage.inputTokens` (DeepSeek excludes cache hits from this field) |
| cache hit | `usage.cacheReadTokens` |
| output | `usage.outputTokens` |
| total | uncached + cache hit + output (+ `cacheWriteTokens` where a provider reports it) |
| cache-hit rate | cache hit ÷ (uncached + cache hit) |

Two deduplication rules keep the numbers honest:

1. **Fork / seeded sessions** — the log starts with a prefix copied from the parent session, whose usage was already billed there. Only events after `inheritedEventCount` are counted (the latest `session/title` is still read from the whole log).
2. **Subagent sessions** — `header.parentSession` identifies the spawning conversation; sessions are grouped up that chain to the top-most main session and reported as one row.

Persisted sessions are immutable, so each log is read once and cached; live sessions are re-read on every refresh. The first open decompresses and replay-validates every log (roughly 10–20 seconds for 500+ sessions) and reports `{ done, total }` progress while polling quickly; afterwards refreshes only re-read running sessions.

- A DeepSeek Harness Web profile, `dsh >= 0.2.1-rc.2`.
- Host services `sessionQuery`, `webServer`, and `connection` (all present in the shipped Web profile).
The plugin is a normal dsh bundle: it registers one Host row and one client half, and does not override any shipped component.

Open **Plugins → Add plugin → Install third-party plugin** and paste one of:

```
dsh-plugin-session-token-stats
```

The same field also accepts a local directory or a Git URL.

dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/genius-alray/dsh-plugin-session-token-stats
```

After installation, reload the page; a bar-chart entry (**Token stats**) appears at the bottom of the left sidebar.

Both routes are same-origin and owner-authenticated through the Connection service (unauthenticated → `401`; missing Connection service → `403`, fail-closed):

- `GET /session-token-stats/data` — totals, daily buckets, grouped per-session aggregates, scan progress.
- `GET /session-token-stats/live` — CPU / load / memory sample ring (1 Hz, last 120 samples).

```
server.js         Host: log folding, subagent grouping, CPU sampling, the two JSON routes
client.js         Client: main panel + sidebar entry, timeline, table, settings
locale/*.json     Plugin catalog metadata (Chinese / English)
cordis.patch.yml  Inserts this plugin's Host row only

```bash
npm run check   # node --check on both halves
npm test        # node --test tests/
```

Tests need no third-party dependencies. The Host suite drives `apply()` with a synthetic corpus through a fake Cordis context (usage folding, peak/off-peak day buckets, inherited-prefix exclusion, subagent grouping, scan caching, route auth); the Client suite loads the browser bundle with a stub module loader and covers token formatting, cache-hit rate, timeline zero-fill, per-browser preferences, and dictionary parity.

- The first scan of 500+ logs takes a few seconds (decompress + replay validation); later refreshes only re-read running sessions.
- The timeline keeps 120 days; older usage still appears in session rows and totals but not in the daily chart.
- When a parent session is no longer in the local corpus (archived or pruned), its subagent sessions become their own top-most row.
- Titles follow the latest `session/title` event, falling back to the first user message for older logs.
- No cost/budget is shown by design; use the token breakdown if you want to price sessions yourself.
